{{short description|Japanese mathematician}}
{{nihongo|'''Sumio Watanabe'''|渡辺 澄夫|Watanabe Sumio|extra=born 1959}} is a Japanese mathematician and engineer working in [[probability theory]], applied [[algebraic geometry]] and [[Bayesian statistics]]. He is currently{{When|date=February 2023}} a professor at [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]] in the Department of Computational Intelligence and Systems Science.<ref>{{cite web|url =http://watanabe-www.math.dis.titech.ac.jp/users/swatanab/curr_vita.html|title = CV|accessdate=15 June 2018|last = Watanabe|first = Sumio}}</ref> He is the author of the text, Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory, which proposes a generalization of Fisher's [[Regular parametric model|regular statistical theory]] to [[singular statistical model]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iapr.org/members/newsletter/Newsletter10-03/index_files/Page529.htm|author=N. Loménie|accessdate=15 June 2018|title=IAPR Newsletter: Review of Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory}}</ref>
